consensus.title: Missing _evict_oldest method causes AttributeError on cache overflow

responses.content: NO_ISSUES_FOUND: Correct, safe, well-structured, and no simpler version is worth the change.

* [WARNING] STRUCTURE Duplicate _evict_oldest method definition (at class LRUCache)
  - Issue: Two definitions of `_evict_oldest` cause a duplicate function definition error, preventing the class from loading and breaking any code that relies on the cache.
  - Fix: Remove the duplicated method definition, keeping only the existing implementation.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Missing `_evict_oldest` method causes AttributeError on cache overflow (at LRUCache.put calling self._evict_oldest)
  - Issue: The original code in `put()` calls `self._evict_oldest()` when `len(self._items) > self.capacity`, but this method was never defined. When the cache exceeds capacity, an AttributeError would be raised, breaking the cache functionality entirely.
  - Fix: The diff correctly adds the missing `_evict_oldest` method that removes the oldest (least recently used) entry using `popitem(last=False)`.

* [WARNING] ERROR_HANDLING Unnecessary guard in `_evict_oldest` (at _evict_oldest method)
  - Issue: The `if self._items:` check is redundant because `put()` only calls `_evict_oldest()` when `len(self._items) > self.capacity`, guaranteeing the dict is non-empty. While harmless, it adds unnecessary branching.
  - Fix: Remove the guard and call `self._items.popitem(last=False)` directly, or keep it for defensive programming if `_evict_oldest` might be called from other contexts in the future.

NO_ISSUES_FOUND: Correct, safe, well-structured, and no simpler version is worth the change.
